advice: Treat the CodeSignal OA as a speed test. Code fast against the exact public API, get each level's tests passing, and expect later levels to force a refactor. Polish at the end.
Edge cases still matter. A candidate scoring about 770/800 was rejected, so check TTL boundaries, missing keys, and same-timestamp ordering.

Drill the small known question bank: in-memory DB, banking system, cloud file storage, web crawler (then concurrent), stack samples to trace events, file dedup, and the LRU/memoize cache made crash-durable.
Know your language's standard library cold. In Python that means threading, concurrent.futures, asyncio, hashlib, os/pathlib and collections. Practise thread-safe visited sets and clean termination.
After a working first version, expect follow-ups on concurrency, data larger than memory, real-time or streaming input, and persistence (WAL or disk). Rehearse how you'd discuss each.
Prepare seriously for the culture/values round: a specific 'why Anthropic' with a real example, plus your views on AI safety. Reports call it the hardest round.
interview_format: Typical 2025–2026 pipeline: a 90-min CodeSignal OA (one progressive 4-level project; a 6-part variant was reported in June 2026), a 30-min recruiter call, then a 45–60 min live coding screen on CodeSignal, Replit or Colab. That screen is one problem with escalating follow-ups. The virtual onsite has 4–5 rounds of about 1 hour each: 1–2 coding, 1–2 system design, hiring manager, and culture/values. Some 2026 loops add a PR-review round where Claude is available. The focus is practical engineering rather than classic DS&A: stateful APIs that evolve, hashing and file I/O, BFS plus concurrency, caching and durability, and scale follow-ups.

problems.description: Build a key/field store class in levels: SET/GET/DELETE, then filtered/prefix scans, then TTL with timestamps, then history lookups or backup/restore.

topic_weights.why: Almost every reported question is a practical build. Examples are the in-memory DB, banking system, file storage, profiler trace events, dedup with streaming, durable LRU, and PR review. Several sources say 'no leetcode' in the OA.
Hash maps and sets underpin the KV-store OA, file dedup (group by size, then content hash), and the crawler's visited set.
The web crawler is BFS over same-host URLs and is the top dataset problem. It was also reported in Sep 2025 screens and onsites.
Both the stack-samples to trace-events profiler question and Exclusive Time of Functions (dataset) need call-stack reasoning and prefix comparison.
The LRU cache (hash map plus doubly linked list) is the base of a reported onsite question that is extended to memoization and crash durability.
The in-memory DB has prefix-scan levels and a hashtag autocomplete title was reported. Evidence for a trie specifically is thin, so the weight is moderate.
Historical, timestamped lookups in the DB OA can use bisect. Otherwise reports say binary search is not asked.
The tokenizer question uses greedy longest-match, but it is a low-confidence report from aggregators only.
Only the low-confidence 'fair coin from biased coin' phone-screen title points here.

# Anthropic software engineering coding interviews: research report

**About me and the sources.** I'm Claude, and Anthropic makes me. I have no inside knowledge of Anthropic's hiring process or question bank. Everything below comes from public reports.

The search turned up mostly Blind, Glassdoor, LeetCode Discuss, a few personal posts, and many interview-prep sites (PracHub, FastPrep, LinkJob, AceOffer, Hack2Hire, SpaceComplexity, IGotAnOffer). The prep sites sell prep material and don't always show where their reports came from, so I treat their specific numbers as **lower confidence**. My Reddit searches only returned Blind pages, so there are no Reddit threads here. I also hit the search tool's usage limit, so some leads weren't followed up. Dates are as the sources state them; the most recent reports are from mid-to-late 2026.

---

## 1. Interview format

**Typical pipeline (2025–2026 reports).** Several sources describe the same sequence: CodeSignal online assessment → recruiter call (30 min) → coding screen (1 hr) → onsite with about 1 hr coding, 1 hr product/system design, 1 hr hiring manager, 1 hr culture → references. This is from a senior SWE, Mar 2026 (https://prachub.com/interview-experiences/anthropic-senior-software-engineer-interview-experience-referral-product-focused-system-design-and-an-850k-offer). The OA → recruiter → phone screen order matches a Feb 2026 LeetCode Discuss post (https://leetcode.com/discuss/post/7559983/). Some candidates have the recruiter call before the CodeSignal link (https://spacecomplexity.ai/blog/anthropic-phone-screen-interview).

**Online assessment (CodeSignal)**
- 90 minutes. One project in 4 levels; each level unlocks after you pass the previous level's tests and usually forces a refactor. A candidate who failed the OA described it as "a 4-level challenge" and said you have to "completely forget about Big O" to finish in time. That post is about 21 months old, so older than 12 months (https://blog.goncharov.page/i-failed-my-anthropic-interview-and-came-to-tell-you-all-about-it-so-you-dont-have-to).
- Blind, Oct 2025: someone who failed twice said "No leet code though in that round… 4 rounds of things that build on top of each other," and that the time pressure is "insane" (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-interview-szdhw35i).
- Glassdoor names it CodeSignal's "industry coding framework" (https://www.glassdoor.com/Interview/Anthropic-Interview-Questions-E8109027.htm). SpaceComplexity instead says "General Coding Framework" (https://spacecomplexity.ai/blog/anthropic-phone-screen-interview). The two disagree; most sources say Industry.
- **Possible format change:** a 6-part version was reported in June 2026 (https://www.sundeepteki.org/advice/anthropic-codesignal-assessment-guide; https://www.hellointerview.com/guides/anthropic/swe). Check your invitation for the exact format.
- **Scoring (low confidence):**
  - Blind posters have seen maximum scores of 600 and 1000 (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-codesignal-interview-gdclgwkl).
  - One person scored about 770/800 and was still rejected (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-codesignal-experience-aumkcovi).
  - SpaceComplexity claims a cutoff around 835/850 but gives no source (https://spacecomplexity.ai/blog/anthropic-phone-screen-interview).
- Glassdoor (London, senior): test cases come in a read-only file (https://www.glassdoor.com/Interview/Anthropic-Senior-Software-Engineer-Interview-Questions-EI_IE8109027.0,9_KO10,34.htm).

**Live coding / phone screen**
- About 45–60 min, with one problem and a series of follow-ups.
- Platforms reported:
  - CodeSignal as the IDE (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-interview-experience-0bzxoarx; https://www.hack2hire.com/forum/6a8ec028cddc54478ddf3470)
  - Replit (https://prachub.com/interview-experiences/anthropic-staff-software-engineer-interview-experience-a-surprise-extra-round-then-a-downlevel-to-senior)
  - Google Colab, in a 2023 report (https://www.teamblind.com/post/Anthropic-Interview-Experience-Software-Engineer-Role-e7QbATrh)
- HelloInterview says Anthropic's careers guidance lists Google Meet, CodeSignal and Google Colab (https://www.hellointerview.com/guides/anthropic/swe).
- If the invite doesn't mention codesignal.com, it's probably a live interview with a person rather than the automated test (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-interview-advice-854xygjz).

**Onsite (virtual)**
- 4–5 rounds of about 55–60 min:
  - coding (1–2 rounds)
  - system design (1–2 rounds)
  - hiring manager / "experiences and goals"
  - culture/values
  - sometimes a technical project presentation

  Sources: https://www.tryexponent.com/guides/anthropic-software-engineer-interview; https://igotanoffer.com/en/advice/anthropic-software-engineer-interview. A Staff candidate in Sep 2025 had 5 rounds after one was added (https://prachub.com/interview-experiences/anthropic-staff-software-engineer-interview-experience-a-surprise-extra-round-then-a-downlevel-to-senior).
- Two prep sites say failing coding or system design cancels the culture and hiring-manager rounds (https://www.hack2hire.com/blog/anthropic-interview-process-rounds-format-timeline-2026; https://spacecomplexity.ai/blog/anthropic-onsite-interview). I found no first-hand confirmation: **low confidence**.
- A Blind poster said the "experiences and goals" round was a standard hiring-manager interview (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-final-round-experience-and-goals-8z0msm06).

**Languages**
- Python dominates the reports. A Blind poster asked whether Python is required and got no real answer (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-interview-szdhw35i).
- Another poster says to know "the language you chose" and its standard library, and that googling was allowed (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-interview-advice-854xygjz).
- The stack-trace problem in the viral video had C++ starter code (https://github.com/ryanhestin/anthropic-challenge). So there seems to be some language choice. **Medium confidence.**

**AI tools**
- Reports conflict:
  - A 2026 PR-review round gave candidates Claude for the whole round (https://www.fastprep.io/experience/2026-anthropic-software-engineer-onsite-pr-review-round-what-it-tests-2-experien-57w38tp2ce).
  - A Blind commenter described the coding rounds as "don't use AI for this" (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-pre-screen-coding-round-a52n538q).
- Follow whatever your round's instructions say.

---

## 2. Reported questions

There are only a handful of distinct problems. The Feb 2026 LeetCode Discuss poster said the question bank "appears to be very small" (https://leetcode.com/discuss/post/7559983/).

## 3. Practical / non-LeetCode rounds

- **Progressive OA build.** You write one class with an exact public API. Each level adds requirements, such as scans, TTL/timestamps, history lookups, or backup/restore and compression. Hidden or provided tests grade it, and later levels usually make you refactor earlier code. Sources: Goncharov blog, IGotAnOffer, and the FastPrep problems linked in section 2.
- **Concurrency extension.** The web crawler starts single-threaded, and most of the round is making it concurrent. You need thread-safe visited/queue state, reliable termination when all work is done, and a discussion of threads vs processes vs async and of crawling across multiple machines (https://www.1point3acres.com/interview/problems/company/anthropic; https://gist.github.com/nito-Q/3b0e09676de3b1176f85e2db3d09a9ad). InterviewingIO says concurrency comes up in several rounds (https://interviewing.io/anthropic-interview-questions).
- **Real-systems follow-ups.** File dedup goes from batch processing to "more files than fit in memory" to real-time detection. The LRU question goes from a cache to crash-durable persistence (Hack2Hire, LinkJob, linked above).
- **PR review round (new in 2026).** You get four pull requests in a repository you haven't seen, with Claude available. In the general SWE version you pick one PR, improve it, and push an update. FastPrep also notes at least six 2026 onsite reports of other formats: system design rounds where you critique an existing design doc, and coding rounds that start from given code containing a bug (https://www.fastprep.io/experience/2026-anthropic-software-engineer-onsite-pr-review-round-what-it-tests-2-experien-57w38tp2ce). This rests on 2 candidate reports: **medium-low confidence.**
- **Older take-home (over 12 months ago, possibly a research-leaning role).** A 5-hour take-home exploring the Anthropic API, plus a review session (https://blog.goncharov.page/i-failed-my-anthropic-interview-and-came-to-tell-you-all-about-it-so-you-dont-have-to).

## 4. Topic emphasis

**Frequent**
- Stateful class or API design that evolves through levels (OA)
- Hash maps and sets
- BFS / graph traversal (crawler)
- Concurrency: threads, locks, queues, async
- Hashing and file I/O (dedup)
- Caching / LRU and persistence
- Stack and prefix comparison (profiler question)
- String handling
- Scale follow-ups

These fit a Blind summary that the questions involve "real world stuff like IO, concurrency, string manipulation" (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-interview-advice-854xygjz).

**Rare or absent**
- I found no reports of DP, heaps, binary search, or advanced graph algorithms.
- Goncharov said to forget about "heaps, binary searches, and the like" for the OA.
- A 2023 Blind post noted "less emphasis on hard core DS/A knowledge" (https://www.teamblind.com/post/Anthropic-Interview-Experience-Software-Engineer-Role-e7QbATrh).

This conclusion comes from the absence of reports, so it is **medium-low confidence**.

**Difficulty perception is mixed.**
- Some call the onsite coding "not leetcode and it's insane" (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-interview-szdhw35i).
- Others describe LC easy-to-medium multi-step problems (2023 Blind), or say the problems "weren't hard, but there was a lot of code to write" (Staff, Sep 2025).

## 5. Recurring advice

1. **The OA is a speed test.** A Blind poster's update: "it absolutely is a speed test" (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-codesignal-interview-gdclgwkl). Code fast, and save polish for later.
2. **Edge-case correctness matters.** A near-perfect score (about 770/800) was still rejected (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-codesignal-experience-aumkcovi).
3. **Practice the known question bank.** The LeetCode Discuss poster prepared the known questions and got one of them (https://leetcode.com/discuss/post/7559983/).
4. **Know your language's standard library well.** For Python that means threading, concurrent.futures, asyncio, hashlib, os/pathlib, and collections (https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-interview-advice-854xygjz). The 2023 Blind post also says to brush up on Python and basic systems knowledge.
5. **Expect follow-ups after the first solution.** Plan for concurrency, scale, durability and real-time processing (Hack2Hire forum; 1point3acres).
6. **Take the culture/values round seriously.** Reports call it the hardest part. Prepare "why Anthropic" with a specific value and a real example, plus your views on AI safety (https://prachub.com/interview-experiences/anthropic-software-engineer-interview-experience-onsite-loop-with-a-1-on-1-chat-system-design-file-dedup-coding-and-a-culture-round-i-couldnt-read; https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-interview-szdhw35i; https://interviewing.io/anthropic-interview-questions). The recruiter call also covers mission and values (LeetCode Discuss).
7. **Expect uneven candidate experience.** Reports include ghosting, passive interviewers, and rejections without feedback. Glassdoor SWE reviews are about 30% positive, with difficulty 3.6/5 (https://www.glassdoor.com/Interview/Anthropic-Software-Engineer-Interview-Questions-EI_IE8109027.0,9_KO10,27.htm; https://www.teamblind.com/post/anthropic-interview-megathread-6estt896).

**What I couldn't verify:**
- Reddit threads (none came back in search)
- Anthropic's official guidance on AI use in interviews (I hit the search limit before finding it)
- Where the prep sites' report counts come from

Check your invitation emails. Per a 2023 Blind report, the email tells you exactly what to prepare.
